title: Send email
description: Deliver one already-rendered email. The producer owns the recipients, the subject and the body; the consumer owns the sender address, the transport and the delivery record. This schema describes the `data` member of the delivered document; the envelope (id, type, aggregate, tenantId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, data) is described in README.md.

requestId.description: The producer's idempotency key. A repeated requestId never sends twice; a requestId whose delivery already died is retried.

to.description: The recipients. Each becomes its own delivery record, so one bad address cannot hide the others.

fromKey.description: A configuration key, never an address. The address must be verified in the account that sends, so it belongs to the consumer while the display name belongs to the producer.

fromName.description: The display name the recipient sees. Quotes, angle brackets, commas and line breaks are refused so it cannot break out of the display-name position.

replyTo.description: Where a reply goes. The consumer checks it against the resolved sender's allowlist, because an arbitrary reply-to turns a DKIM-valid suite email into business-email compromise.

subject.description: Line breaks are refused: they are the header-injection vector.

List-Unsubscribe.description: An RFC 2369 List-Unsubscribe value, normally an angle-bracketed URL. Line breaks are refused: they are the header-injection vector.

headers.description: Extra transport headers, restricted to an allowlist of two names. Marketing mail needs List-Unsubscribe; nothing else does, and an open map would let a producer set arbitrary headers and rewrite the message's meaning. Omitted entirely by notification.
